editorial:
Imagine having a crush on your next-door neighbor for twenty whole years. That is exactly where you find Kaede, who has been head-over-heels for Haru since they were four years old. The vibe here is super cozy and sweet, focusing on that awkward space between being best friends and wanting something more. You get to see Kaede struggle with her feelings while her friends give her advice on whether to keep trying or finally move on. It feels like a warm hug of a movie, capturing those relatable moments of longing and the fear of ruining a great friendship.

What really makes this work is the slow build-up of tension when a third guy, Iori, enters the picture. The acting feels natural and not over-the-top, which makes the emotional scenes hit harder. While the pace is a bit slow at times, the payoff is worth it. If you are into slow-burn romances, you should definitely check this out. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the pretty scenery, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you like keeping physical copies of your favorite comfort movies.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Haru finally admits his true feelings. You find out he was holding back because of a promise he made to Kaede's late mother to protect and look after her. Once he realizes he might lose her to Iori, he stops hiding. Haru and Kaede finally confess their love for each other and decide to start dating, ending their two-decade wait with a happy, romantic connection.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves childhood-friends-to-lovers stories and cute Japanese dramas.
